question: A company designs a new chocolate box in the shape of a regular right pyramid with a square base. The base side of the box is 10 cm and its height is 12 cm. Due to packaging constraints, the box can only be filled up to 90% of its total volume. If the company wants to estimate the total cost of chocolate, knowing that 1 cm³ of chocolate costs ₹0.50, what is the cost of chocolate to fill one such box?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Volume = (1/3) × a² × h = (1/3) × 100 × 12 = 400 cm³

Filled Volume (90%) = 0.9 × 400 = 360 cm³

Total Cost = 360 × 0.50 = ₹180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base side (a) = 10 cm

Height (h) = 12 cm

Volume filled = 90%

Cost of chocolate = ₹0.50 per cm³

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a Pyramid = (1/3) × Base Area × Height
